description: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.) is a global fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with a worldwide footprint spanning subsidiaries in over 20 countries including Armenia, Barbados, Belgium, Bermuda, Brazil, Canada, China, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK. The company generates 66-71% of its net revenue from international markets, with significant revenue contributions from the United States ($8.7B), China/Hong Kong ($6.2B), Singapore ($3.6B), Taiwan ($3.3B), Japan ($1.8B), and Europe ($1.6B) in FY2024. AMD employs approximately 31,000 people globally and operates through segments including Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded, serving customers across North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe.

revenueGeography.reason: Prioritizing the most recent quarterly data (Q1 2026 ended March 28, 2026) as the anchor filing. AMD does not provide a detailed geographic revenue breakdown in its quarterly earnings releases; the most recent detailed geographic revenue data available is from FY2024 (annual SEC filing) which shows United States $8.7B, China $6.2B, Singapore $3.6B, Taiwan $3.3B, Japan $1.8B, Europe $1.6B, Other $0.6B. For Q1 2026, total GAAP revenue is $10.3B. The FY2024 geographic percentages are applied as a proxy for the latest period, with the note that international sales were 66% of net revenue in FY2024. Q1 2026 also includes ~$100M AMD Instinct MI308 sales to China.

geopoliticalRisks.description: BIS export controls since Oct 2023 prevent AMD from shipping Instinct MI308 and Versal FPGAs to China without license. April 2025 new license requirements for D5 countries. Q2 2025: ~$800M inventory charges on MI308. Full year 2025: ~$440M net charges. August 2025: AMD agreed to pay U.S. government 15% of AI chip sale revenues from China as MI308 license condition, raising constitutional concerns under Article I, Section 9, Clause 5. January 2026 BIS rule reviews MI325X on case-by-case basis. China accounted for 22% ($5,207M) of AMD's net revenue in fiscal 2022.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: AMD 10-K FY2022; AMD 10-Q Q2/Q3/Q4 2025; CRS Report August 2025; BIS Rule January 13, 2026

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: TSMC Manufacturing Concentration & Taiwan Strait Risk
geopoliticalRisks.description: AMD depends entirely on TSMC for all advanced-node wafer production (7nm or smaller). Any disruption at TSMC due to geopolitical conflict between China and Taiwan could materially adversely affect AMD's business. Taiwan experienced earthquake in April 2024 where AMD's third-party wafer foundries are located. AMD's Taiwan-based third-party wafer foundries, manufacturing facilities, and subcontractors are at risk from geopolitical changes between China and Taiwan.

January 2025: BIS issued AI Diffusion Rule. May 13, 2025: BIS rescinded Biden AI Diffusion Rule and instructed enforcement officials not to enforce. May 2025: BIS announced intention to rescind and issue replacement rules. January 13, 2026: BIS issued new rule revising licensing policy for semiconductor exports to China. This regulatory volatility creates persistent uncertainty for AMD's product roadmap and revenue planning. BIS also closed VEU program loophole (Aug 2025) and issued entity ownership rule (Sep 2025, enforcement suspended until Nov 2026).
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: BIS AI Diffusion Rule Jan 2025; BIS Rescission May 13, 2025; BIS Rule Jan 13, 2026; BIS VEU Rule Aug 29, 2025

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: THATIC Joint Venture Entity List Sanctions
geopoliticalRisks.description: June 2019: BIS added THATIC and THATIC JV (AMD's joint venture with Higon Information Technology Co., Ltd.) to Entity List. AMD has equity interests in two joint ventures with Higon (Chinese entity on Entity List). AMD may not realize expected benefits including milestone payments and royalties. China's SAMR set restrictive conditions on AMD's acquisition of Xilinx in 2022 as part of antitrust review approvals.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: AMD 10-K FY2022; BIS Entity List June 2019

geopoliticalRisks.description: Worsening U.S.-China trade relationship could negatively impact AMD's worldwide operations. U.S. has imposed/proposed higher tariffs on imports; China has imposed retaliatory tariffs. Retaliatory actions by affected countries could result in tariffs/restrictions on AMD's products. Data center hardware infrastructure costs may increase for AMD's customers due to tariffs, potentially causing delays/halts in AI infrastructure investments.

U.S. and other countries issued sanctions and export control revisions against Russia, Belarus, DNR/LNR regions of Ukraine. AMD (including Xilinx) suspended shipments to Russian Federation during fiscal quarter ended March 26, 2022. Xilinx had authorized third-party resellers in Russia filing notifications with Russian FSB (U.S.-designated blocked party under Executive Order 13382). Ukraine-Russia conflict escalation could negatively impact global economy.

March 25, 2025: BIS added 80 entities to Entity List from China, UAE, South Africa, Iran, Taiwan (12 for developing advanced AI/supercomputers/AI chips). This expands restrictions affecting AMD's supply chain and partner ecosystem in Taiwan.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: EU AI Act & GDPR Compliance Burden
geopoliticalRisks.description: EU AI Act (adopted 2024, phased implementation) may impede AMD's ability to offer certain products/services in EU. New/proposed AI legislation could impact AMD's ability to sell AI-related products and reduce customer base. EU GDPR imposes significant requirements on personal data collection/processing with significant fines. EU enacted restrictions on lead and other materials in electronic products affecting semiconductor devices/packaging.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: EU AI Act 2024; EU GDPR; AMD 10-K FY2022

geopoliticalRisks.description: Deemed export restrictions could affect AMD's ability to provide services/develop products in U.S. with non-U.S. personnel. New export controls may adversely impact AMD's R&D teams located outside U.S. from executing product roadmaps. BIS expands licensing requirements worldwide for transactions involving entities/end uses associated with AI capabilities development/proliferation.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: AMD 10-K FY2022 Risk Factors; BIS Rules 2025-2026

geopoliticalRisks.description: U.S. Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act prohibits goods from Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region under presumption of forced labor. Germany, UK, Australia, California enacted laws requiring AMD to disclose forced labor/human trafficking elimination policies in supply chain. Customers and governments focus on eliminating forced labor risks, increasing AMD's compliance costs.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act; AMD 10-K FY2022

geopoliticalRisks.description: Israel-Hamas conflict could escalate and negatively impact global economy and financial markets. While AMD does not have disclosed material direct operations in Israel, broader regional instability could affect global semiconductor supply chains and financial conditions.
